title: Rethinking Positional Encoding and Interaction Granularity for CTR Prediction
abstract: arXiv:2610.37140v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Click-through rate (CTR) prediction relies on historical behaviors and contextual features to estimate clicks on a target item. Existing Transformer-based CTR models often adopt index-based or temporal positional encodings and token-level causal interaction. However, we observe that most existing positional encodings do not outperform NoPE, while relaxing causal constraints within target-relative temporal groups also yields gains. These observations motivate a fundamental question: what positional encoding and interaction granularity does CTR prediction actually require? To address this question, we propose \textbf{TRIP}, which combines target-aware rank--time positional encoding with temporal-group interaction modeling. Specifically, Factorized Rank Encoding represents each behavior's ordinal position within the historical sequence through a low-rank factorization, while Target-Relative Time Encoding characterizes its temporal distance

translated_title: 重新思考CTR预测中的位置编码与交互粒度
translated_abstract: 点击率（CTR）预测依靠历史行为和上下文特征来估计用户对目标物品的点击。现有基于Transformer的CTR模型通常采用基于索引或时间的位置编码以及token级别的因果交互。然而，我们观察到大多数现有位置编码的性能并不优于NoPE（无位置编码），而放宽目标相对时间组内的因果约束也能带来性能提升。这些观察引发了一个根本性问题：CTR预测究竟需要什么样的位置编码和交互粒度？为了回答这一问题，我们提出了TRIP，它将目标感知的秩-时间位置编码与时间组交互建模相结合。具体而言，因子化秩编码通过低秩因子分解表示每个行为在历史序列中的序数位置，而目标相对时间编码则刻画其与目标物品的时间距离
tldr: 提出TRIP模型，将目标感知的秩-时间位置编码与时间组交互建模相结合，揭示了大多数现有位置编码并不优于无位置编码，从而重新思考了CTR预测真正所需的位置编码与交互粒度。
en_tdlr: TRIP combines target-aware rank-time positional encoding with temporal-group interaction modeling, revealing that most existing positional encodings do not outperform NoPE and rethinking what positional encoding and interaction granularity CTR prediction actually requires.
